shortName: East Tennessee State University James H. Quillen College of Medicine

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: Quillen welcomes applications from groups underrepresented in medicine, those with past or present military service, those from rural and underserved areas, LGBTQI, and those coming from disadvantaged socioeconomic or educational backgrounds. University committees work collaboratively with colleagues from the East Tennessee State University and ETSU Health to create meaningful programs and initiatives to foster a supportive community where students from all walks of life can thrive academically and professionally. This focus extends to the curriculum, with an emphasis on addressing healthcare disparities and preparing students to serve various populations.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students may be placed on leave of absence based on their request or by direction of appropriate institutional officials or bodies.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Quillen offers a wide range of student organizations and activities to enhance both personal and professional development. Students can participate in medical interest groups, advocacy organizations, and special interest groups. There are opportunities for community service, leadership, networking, and research interests. Social and recreational activities are encouraged as well, with events like sports leagues, wellness programs, and cultural celebrations. Additionally, the area abounds with plentiful opportunities for hiking, camping, watersports, concerts, plays, lectures and other cultural events to enrich the lives of our students. These opportunities create a well-rounded experience throughout the duration of students' time at Quillen.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Located in one of Tennessee's largest metro areas, Quillen is in a unique setting providing accessibility to both city amenities and the natural beauty and peacefulness of the mountain landscapes, small towns, and rural communities of East Tennessee, Southwest Virginia, Southeast Kentucky, and Western North Carolina.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Quillen students have a variety of housing options to suit their needs. Campus housing is available for those who prefer a convenient living arrangement, offering modern apartments and dorm-style accommodations. These options are located near the college, providing easy access to classes and campus facilities.  Off-campus housing is abundant in the surrounding areas, including apartments, rental homes, and shared housing options in nearby communities with public transportation available or just minutes from the campus in a more rural setting.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Quillen promotes a culture of respect and inclusion in all settings fostering a space where all students can feel welcome and supported.  Students can connect with groups, such as the LGBTQ+ student organization, for community, advocacy, and resources and the college offers a safe, inclusive environment through initiatives like LGBTQ+ awareness programs and access to counseling services that are sensitive to the needs of gender and sexual minority students.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Quillen is committed to providing equitable access for all students. The university main campus Disability Services office oversees the accommodation process, while facilitation and guidance for Quillen students is provided through Counseling and Academic Resource Essential Services (CARES).
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: As part of a robust wellness program, Quillen College of Medicine is committed to monitoring students and gaining feedback on how to provide consistently superior support and promote student wellness.  The Office of Student Affairs offers direction and resources that cover holistic wellness (emotional, physical, intellectual, community, spiritual, social, financial  and occupational/career health).
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The campus culture at Quillen College of Medicine is one of collaboration, support, and community engagement. Students are encouraged to work together in a team-based environment, fostering strong peer relationships and academic success. The college values creating an environment where all backgrounds are respected. With a focus on clinical training, particularly in rural and underserved communities, students gain hands-on experience early in their education. Faculty are approachable and dedicated to mentoring students, while research opportunities allow students to engage in meaningful work, especially related to health disparities. Quillen’s culture promotes both academic and personal growth, preparing students to become compassionate, well-rounded physicians.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Students must have readily available transportation to off campus sites, especially in the clinical years.  It is highly recommended that they are licensed drivers with their own vehicle for this purpose.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Students should dress in a manner that is appropriate for the particular educational setting and that reflects professionalism in dealing with faculty, staff, patients, and the public.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: All students are provided with academic assistance as necessary to include tutors and/or professional counseling designed to maximize the students' academic and personal success
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students receive early clinical training in physical examination and patient communication with real, standardized, and simulated patients in the first year.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Team-Based Learning, Case-Based Learning, Interactive and integrated content, emphasis on formative assessment
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Core clerkships are during the third year with electives in the senior year.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The TRAILS (Team-based Rural Applied Integrated Learning System) curriculum includes the integration of basic and clinical sciences, opportunities for early clinical experiences, state-of-the-art interprofessional training and simulation, and multiple service learning and community outreach opportunities. The curriculum is delivered in learning environments that engage faculty and students in the active application of knowledge and the practice of skills central to patient care.  Patient contact comes early in the curriculum and continues throughout.  Flexibility is allowed for students to decelerate a portion of the curriculum for elective opportunities, including research and advanced clinical studies, or dual degree programs (MD/MPH, MD/MBA).
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Quillen maintains its long-term mission and commitment to excellence in preparing physicians who are likely to engage in primary care or rural medicine. A Rural Primary Care Track (RPCT) covering parts of all four years is available to a portion of each entering class.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
The Medical Student Summer Research Program is offered to rising second year medical students. Selected students spend approximately six weeks during the summer between their first and second years working on a basic science or a clinical research project. They then give a presentation of their research at the Medical Student Research Symposium in the first semester of the second year. Students are also encouraged to present their findings at the Appalachian Student Research Forum at ETSU as well as any local or national conferences.

For more information about research at Quillen, visit https://www.etsu.edu/com/research.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Students are active in community service through Learning Communities and numerous other opportunities available.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Rising second-year students may participate in the Summer Research Program, and can also engage in meaningful research supported by mentorship and institutional resources.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Hospital and clinic affiliations throughout the Tri-Cities and adjacent region listed at https://www.etsu.edu/com/aboutus/affiliates.php
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Mixed; all courses in the pre-clerkship phase are graded as Pass/Fail.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Opening in 1978, ETSU Quillen College of Medicine is a national leader in primary care and rural medicine. The college boasts a high national residency match success rate, with over 50% of graduates pursuing careers in primary care. Quillen's Community Partnerships Program and Rural Primary Care Track have earned national acclaim. The school fosters a collegial environment where student input is highly valued. The primary medical campus, located on the VA Medical Center grounds, features one of the nation’s most advanced patient simulation programs, complemented by the Standardized Patient Program. Situated in one of Tennessee’s largest metro areas, Quillen is part of the state’s fourth-largest university, with approximately 14,000 students each year. It is supported by modern medical centers and clinics across the Tri-Cities, providing students with extensive clinical training opportunities.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The primary mission of the Quillen College of Medicine is to educate and train future physicians, particularly those interested in primary care, to serve in underserved rural communities. The College is also dedicated to advancing biomedical research and improving healthcare in Northeast Tennessee and the broader Appalachian region.

As a leading healthcare provider in East Tennessee, Quillen strives to meet community and regional health needs by identifying, creating, and implementing programs that leverage its resources. In alignment with this responsibility, the College emphasizes primary care as the core focus of its medical practice and training programs. The selection process prioritizes candidates with a demonstrated interest in rural and primary care, ensuring that the college’s mission remains at the forefront.

Quillen fosters its mission by engaging with schools across the state through ongoing campus visits and outreach programs. The College offers programs like the Extending Quillen to the Underserved through an Integrated Program (EQUIP) for high school and college students, as well as the Tri-Trails Program, which accelerates training for those interested in family medicine, internal medicine, or pediatrics. The College boasts an experienced and dedicated faculty in the biological, behavioral, and clinical sciences, complemented by practicing physicians who serve as part-time and volunteer faculty members.

In addition to rigorous academic training, Quillen provides learning communities and extensive counseling services to support student well-being and development. These communities foster smaller group environments that promote health, wellness, and engagement in community service projects. Quillen students also actively participate in local health fairs and outreach activities, particularly in rural areas, further enhancing their commitment to serving underserved populations.

As a result of these initiatives, over 50% of Quillen graduates pursue primary care residencies, with many choosing to practice in rural and underserved areas. The majority of Quillen graduates remain in Tennessee to practice, with many returning to the communities they were trained to serve, continuing the College’s mission of improving healthcare across the region.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Additional letters may also be submitted (such as from an employer, mentor or physician) but should be kept to a minimum and should provide information not otherwise available to the committee. All evaluations must be submitted via AMCAS Letter Service.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Quillen does not require an evaluation from a pre-professional advisory committee, but recommends one if such a committee exists at the undergraduate institution. Institutions differ in the way they prepare pre-professional evaluations and if the applicant’s school/advisor prepares a standard set of credentials these will be accepted in lieu of a committee evaluation.  Otherwise, an applicant may provide a minimum of three evaluations from faculty members, advisors, or others who are most familiar with the applicant’s academic abilities (especially in the sciences), leadership, problem-solving skills, altruism, communication skills or ability to function as a member of a team.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: For the 2026-2027 application year, all interviews and informational sessions will be conducted virtually. Information and instructions regarding interviews will be provided to selected applicants.  Applicants will first attend a virtual information session with admissions and financial services staff on a afternoon prior to the interview day.  The interview day consists of two semi-structured interviews with members of the admissions committee.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two one-on-one, semi-structured interviews with admissions committee members.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: All interviews for the 2026-2027 application year will be virtual.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Following  an initial review, selected applicants may be requested to submit a secondary application. Notification will be sent by email.
medSchoolApplication.secApplLatestDtText: Application/fee must be submitted within seven days.  Recommendations and Casper scores to be submitted asap. All evaluations and scores must be in by January 15, 2027 latest to be considered.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: Both early decision and regular decision applicants are held to the same high standards of admission; early decision applicants are not given preference over regular applicants.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Quillen College of Medicine’s Admission Protocols policy:
All applicants holding acceptance to Quillen are expected to comply fully and professionally with all AAMC Admissions Protocols and are required to formally indicate their intention of enrolling at Quillen by selecting the “Commit to Enroll” selection through the AMCAS “Chose Your Medical School Tool” at a date no later than 38 days prior to the first day of orientation or other required attendance at Quillen. All will additionally be required to formally notify Quillen that they are in compliance with this protocol and that they have withdrawn all other applications, no matter what the status of that application, from all other allopathic, osteopathic and Texas medical schools for the current year. Those not in timely compliance with this policy may have their acceptance to Quillen immediately withdrawn and that class position offered to another applicant.

https://www.etsu.edu/com/admissions/requirements/admissions-protocols.php
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The committee reviews all visible scores within the last THREE years prior to application (January 2023 through September 12, 2026 for the 2026-2027 cycle).
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: Applications with MCAT scores below 497 will not be deemed competitive for further consideration.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: There is no minimum required GPA for consideration of postbacc or graduate coursework. All visible coursework information is taken into consideration.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: There are no minimum credit hours required for consideration of postbacc or graduate coursework; however, in the case of a lower undergraduate GPA, there must be enough postbacc or graduate coursework information available to show increasing academic capability in higher level courses.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Completion of a minimum of 90 semester hours of coursework from regionally accredited U.S. institution(s) is required for admission. This includes work completed at community colleges.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Letters of intent, interest, and updates are acceptable.  These can be submitted to the Admissions office at sacom@etsu.edu.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
Quillen College of Medicine’s listed technical standards inform incoming and enrolled students of the abilities and characteristics that are necessary to successfully complete the requirements of the medical education curriculum and provide effective and safe care.  In order to matriculate, candidates must meet these technical standards, with or without reasonable accommodations, and maintain related satisfactory demonstration of these standards for progression through the program. 

The technical standards were developed in accordance with LCME and legal standards, including Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act and Title III of the Americans with Disabilities Act. 

These ensure that applicants and enrolled students with disabilities are not discriminated against based on disability and are provided an equal, effective, and meaningful opportunity to enjoy the benefits, privileges, and advantages of a medical education.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: The need for student financial assistance is not a consideration in the selection process. Institutional scholarships and grants are available, as are loans for those students who demonstrate need as defined by a federal needs analysis and who meet the specific criteria set forth by the various agencies. Specific financial information is provided during pre-interview information sessions and by visiting the Office of Financial Services website at https://www.etsu.edu/com/sa/comfinaid
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: All students enrolled are required by the Tennessee Board of Regents to pay tuition and fees at the beginning of each academic period before attending any class, clerkship or curricular session.

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: Tri-TRAILS students complete first three years with students in the 4-year program. They have the addition of eight weeks clinical experiences between year one and two and complete their pre-clerkship preceptor experience with faculty in chosen residency program. After the required year three clerkships, students take USMLE Step 2 CK, participate in Keystone experience and complete required sub-internship and ICU experience. This satisfies all graduation requirements before the end year three.
medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants: Students who are interested in Tri-TRAILS must first be accepted to the Quillen College of Medicine.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Applicants not immediately accepted or rejected will be placed on active hold/waitlist until further action is taken. Prompt notification is provided of any changes.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Applicants are encouraged to pursue their own intellectual interests in completing a broadly based undergraduate education demonstrating scholastic rigor, analytic and critical thinking, an aptitude for understanding complex systems in human biology, and the ability to apply knowledge. Although Quillen does not requires the completion of any specific courses at the undergraduate level, adequate preparation in both the hard sciences and social/behavioral sciences is strongly recommended. Completion of a minimum of 90 semester hours of coursework from a regionally accredited college or university is required to be eligible for admission. Undergraduate GPA, strength of curriculum and scores on the MCAT will continue to be evaluated as important indicators of probable academic success.
https://www.etsu.edu/com/admissions/requirements/academic-requirements.php
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
Admission is based upon a competitive selection process involving those applicants who meet the minimum requirements for admission https://www.etsu.edu/com/admissions/requirements/application-information.php
The Admissions Committee screens applicants on the basis of academic preparedness and achievement, MCAT scores, Casper scores (Acuity Insights), letters of recommendation, pertinent extracurricular research and work experiences, evidence of non-scholastic accomplishments and demonstrated passion for the profession. Undergraduate GPA, strength of curriculum and scores on the MCAT will continue to be evaluated as important indicators of probable academic success. Additionally, the Admissions Committee selects students who give the promise of being not merely satisfactory medical students, but also capable, responsible, professional physicians of high ethical standards.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Each application is examined for evidence of an applicant’s firsthand exposure to health care as an indication that the applicant is familiar with the realities of medicine as a career. The Admissions Committee seeks demonstrations that the applicant has made a serious and reasoned commitment to the attainment of goals commensurate with those of the institution and the profession. Those experiences demonstrating leadership, altruism, high achievement and dedication to service are particularly valued.
